title: Rappolo's playing and Charlie Cardello
summary: Opinions on Rappolo as reader and clarinetist, and his brother's threat at a recording session.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: No. No, huh? No, he couldn't read it. No big as a bass player.
How did he play a sax? Did you like his sax style?
Well, he played all right, but I heard better. You liked his clarinet playing?
Have you ever heard him and Charlie Cardello wait together? No.
Never have. No, I don't think I have. I don't remember it.

Because those were the last records that Rap was on with the Halfway House, you see. Uh-huh. And that's when Charlie was telling me some cute things that happened with Rap. Uh-huh. That he got mad and didn't show up for a session. They had a recording session, you know? Yeah.

And Rap's brother came down there with a gun on his hip and he told Cardello, who was going to play clarinet instead of Rapolo. Uh-huh. Says, if you copy any of his style, I'll be standing out here waiting for you.
Well, you see, that gives you some slight idea of how, uh, of how serious they were about musicians and the music played.
